name: Belgium
blurb: Chocolate, beer, comic art and medieval squares.
cities: The Grand-Place, Art Nouveau facades and moules-frites.
Canals and a perfectly preserved medieval centre.
Medieval guildhalls and a lively student scene.
Medieval civic bell towers, with Ghent's belfry as the classic climb.
19th-century farm colonies built to lift poor families out of poverty.
Quiet walled courtyards where religious women lived together in the Middle Ages.
Flanders Fields cemeteries, the Menin Gate and the nightly Last Post.
Coal mines and workers' towns, including the grand Grand-Hornu complex.
Art Nouveau town houses by Victor Horta, with flowing iron and stained glass.
Neolithic flint mines dug 6,000 years ago, open for underground visits.
A five-towered Romanesque and Gothic cathedral in one of Belgium's oldest cities.
The world's oldest printing presses, in a Renaissance printing house in Antwerp.
A Vienna Secession mansion with a Klimt frieze, seen only from the street.
A Le Corbusier studio house in Antwerp's suburbs.
Historic hydraulic boat lifts on a canal you can still cruise.
The original spa town, with thermal baths, forest walks and the Francorchamps circuit.
